description:
The /fly HUD speed readout displays 'NaN km/s' during outer-planet missions (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) for the entire outbound cruise after the spacecraft passes ~2.5 AU from the Sun

Expected: The HUD speed readout should show the spacecraft's actual heliocentric speed in km/s while traversing the transfer orbit to any destination

Acceptance criteria:
- Galileo at cruise midpoint (~3.1 AU from Sun in Earth→Jupiter Hohmann) shows ~11.2 km/s, not NaN [code-invariant: NaN is never a valid display value. Expected value computable from vis-viva with a=(1.0+5.20336)/2=3.10168 AU (planets.json: Earth a=1.0, Jupiter a=5.20336)]
- Cassini at cruise midpoint (~5.3 AU, Earth→Saturn Hohmann) shows ~8.5 km/s, not NaN [code-invariant: NaN is never a valid display value. a from planets.json: Saturn a=9.53707]
- Voyager 2 (Jupiter→Saturn→Uranus→Neptune grand tour) does not show NaN at any point [code-invariant: NaN is never a valid display value]
- New Horizons (Pluto) does not show NaN during its Jupiter gravity-assist or post-Jupiter cruise [code-invariant: NaN is never a valid display value]
- Earth→Mars missions continue to show valid speed values unchanged (regression guard) [baseline: Existing behaviour for Mars missions must not regress]

Domain facts:
- Vis-viva: v = √(µ · (2/r − 1/a)). NaN occurs when r > 2a (negative radicand).
- Correct a for each destination's Hohmann transfer is (R_Earth + R_dest) / 2, stored per planet in planets.json.
